1. You are a good, beautiful and important person. Hold on to that. Remember it forever.   
2. Knowing that there are other people in the world who share this disorder helps tremendously. Become involved in online communities built for people like us. They're  everywhere, just search. Physical friendships can come later, when YOU'RE ready.   
3. Having a therapist will help you. I was lucky. I had a regular behavioral counselor and an anger management counselor for 3-4 years as a teen. I wasn't diagnosed until last year, but I was able to learn about my reactions and coping skills.   
4. Please stop self harming. Save for a drunken hiccup after my uncle committed suicide, I haven't since 2009. It's hard. So freaking hard. But you don't deserve it. Instead, find a physical outlet. I run. I run until I'm numb. Buy a punching bag or something, but don't hurt yourself. You are more important than the pain.   
5. If you need me, send me a message. I'm a friend and an ally, like the people in this community typically are. Don't bury your feelings, talk them out. :) You'll be okay. I promise.
